title: The Avocado Paradox: Algorithmic Homogenization, Collective Hedonic Adaptation and Collapse of Conversational Novelty in Contemporary Adulthood
content: Contemporary adults report declining social excitement, weakening conversational motivation and a sense of emotional flattening within peer groups, even with the sheer amount of experiential currency available around. This paper argues that this paradox arises not from individual habituation alone, but from what this paper proposes as Collective Hedonic Adaptation (CHA). Experiential homogenization (EH) across social groups systematically depletes the Interpersonal Information Utility (IIU) of shared narratives. This paper introduces the Avocado Paradox framework, integrating Hedonic Adaptation Prevention (HAP) theory, Optimal Distinctiveness Theory (ODT) and Socioemotional Selectivity Theory (SST) into a unified conceptual model linking Experiential Saturation (ES) to declining Conversational Novelty (CN), Social Engagement Quality (SEQ), Perceived Life Excitement (PLE) and Subjective Well-Being (SWB). Six propositions are advanced including Algorithmic Curation as a historically novel accelerant of narrative capital collapse. Implications for consumer experience design, brand differentiation strategy, and well-being research are discussed.
